 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Former MLB player and Mansfield High standout Sam Hilliard has reached the sport's biggest stage — in South Korea.
 The 32-year-old Hilliard has helped power the KT Wiz to the Korean Series, the Korean Baseball Organization's version of the World Series. The top-seeded Wiz will host the No. 2 Samsung Lions in Game 1 of the best-of-7 series at 3:30 a.m. Central time Tuesday. The games will not be on American TV.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The 6-foot-5, 235-pound Hilliard has quickly excelled in his first season in the KBO after seven seasons in the majors with the Colorado Rockies and Atlanta Braves. The outfielder leads the league with 139 RBIs and is second in home runs with 44. He is batting .304 with a .593 slugging percentage in 142 games.
 In 332 MLB games, Hilliard hit .218 with 44 home runs and 107 RBIs, slugging .437.
 After graduating from Mansfield, Hilliard went to two junior colleges before spending a season at Wichita State. He was taken by the Rockies in the 15th round of the 2015 MLB draft.
 Mansfield pitcher Sam Hilliard during a game against Mansfield Legacy on April 13, 2012, at Mansfield High.
